key_insight: Ceramic performance is controlled by the chain from atomic bonding and processing to microstructure and, ultimately, mechanical, thermal, electrical, and biomedical properties.
engineering_relevance: The review shows how processing choices such as sintering, sol--gel, and additive manufacturing can tune density, porosity, phase stability, and functionality in advanced ceramic components and implants.
method: Conventional sintering to increase densification and control grain growth
Sol--gel processing for composition and microstructure control
Additive manufacturing for complex geometry and tailored porosity
evidence_signal: This is a narrative review that synthesizes prior studies on structure--property relationships, biomedical ceramic classes, and processing routes rather than presenting a new dataset or benchmark.
watch_item: Ceramics remain vulnerable to brittle fracture, flaw sensitivity, and the porosity--strength trade-off, so improved processing must balance performance with reliability.
paper_title: Ceramic Materials: From Atomic Bonding and Processing to Microstructure, Functional Properties, and Biomedical Applications
